name: managed-oauth-vs-mcp-remote
query: I have an MCP server running on ECS, fronted by Cloudflare Access with Google SSO. Users currently configure it in Claude Desktop using mcp-remote as a stdio proxy that does the OAuth dance to Cloudflare. Can I drop mcp-remote so the client connects natively?
expected_behavior: Says YES — enable Managed OAuth on the cloudflare_zero_trust_access_application: oauth_configuration { enabled = true, dynamic_client_registration { enabled = true, allow_any_on_localhost = true, allow_any_on_loopback = true } }. That makes the Access app publish /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, /authorize, /token, and DCR registration at the upstream hostname.

Explains that with those endpoints present, Claude Desktop / claude.ai web / Claude Code discover OAuth on the upstream and run the flow natively — mcp-remote is no longer needed in the client config.

Notes DCR is required (Claude clients register dynamically; no static-client UI) and allow_any_on_localhost/allow_any_on_loopback are required for Claude Desktop's http://127.0.0.1:<random-port>/callback.
Tells the user to verify with `curl https://<host>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server | jq .` — should return issuer + authorization_endpoint + token_endpoint + registration_endpoint.
Does NOT recommend writing custom OAuth in the MCP origin.
Does NOT suggest the Workers OAuth Provider library (that's for origins running ON Workers, not behind Access).
